WS-001.source: Met object page 329081 (Provenance tab) and Met API
WS-001.provenance_text: Until 1988, Erlenmeyer collection, purchased by Professor Hans and Marie-Louise Erlenmeyer between 1943 and the early 1960s; acquired by the Museum in 1988, purchased at the sale of Ancient Near Eastern texts form the Erlenmeyer collection, Christie's, London, December 13, 1988, lot 21
WS-001.basis: In a documented private collection outside Iraq before 1970 (bought 1943 to early 1960s)
WS-001.gap: How and when it left Iraq is not recorded

WS-090.provenance_text: Until 1988, Erlenmeyer collection, purchased by Professor Hans and Marie-Louise Erlenmeyer between 1943 and the early 1960s; acquired by the Museum in 1988, purchased at the sale of Ancient Near Eastern texts form the Erlenmeyer collection, Christie's, London, December 13, 1988 [lot number truncated in the page summary]
WS-090.basis: Same collection and sale as WS-001
WS-090.gap: How and when it left Iraq is not recorded

WS-007.provenance_text: [André Emmerich Gallery, New York, 1960s]; Guido and Nelly di Tella, Buenos Aires, ca. 1960s–2013; Claudia Quentin, New York, 2013–2021
WS-007.basis: Outside Peru by the 1960s on the museum's record; the Met brackets the 1960s gallery step, which marks it as unconfirmed
WS-007.gap: Findspot unknown; the pre-1970 step is bracketed

WS-043.provenance_text: Emil Brugsch-Bey (until 1890; sold to Baker); George F. Baker, New York (1890; gifted to MMA)
WS-043.gap: Findspot unknown. The seller worked for Egypt's antiquities service; sales like this were legal then, which F1.24 can question

WS-060.provenance_text: Frank Caro [1904–1980], New York, NY, given to the Cleveland Museum of Art by exchange (?–1960); The Cleveland Museum of Art (1960–)
WS-060.gap: History before Frank Caro not recorded

WS-081.provenance_text: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Cleveland, OH (1970—) [entry 1 not published]
WS-081.basis: Accessioned 9 March 1970, eight months before the 17 November 1970 threshold
WS-081.gap: Earlier owners not published; the record's first entry is missing

WS-092.provenance_text: Mrs. Christian R. Holmes; Mozaffar Cohen, Paris [no dates]
WS-092.basis: In Cleveland since 1961; two named earlier owners
WS-092.gap: No findspot; Luristan bronzes as a group were mostly dug without record from 1928

WS-053.provenance_text: [none published]; credit line Gift of John Wise, accessioned 30 October 1940

WS-012.provenance_text: Mr. and Mrs. Robert M. Hornung, Cleveland Heights, OH, given to the Cleveland Museum of Art (?–1962)
WS-012.gap: How it left Ghana is not recorded

WS-005.provenance_text: (Gallery Kapitan, Tokyo, Japan, sold to the Cleveland Museum of Art) (?–1984); The Cleveland Museum of Art (1984–)
WS-005.basis: First record 1984; no excavation or export record published
WS-005.gap: Also: the museum reports that a base from a different vessel was used in a 20th-century reconstruction
WS-005.action: Case, not exemplar: what a reconstruction and a missing history each hide. Replace the exemplar with an excavated flame vessel held in Japan (ColBase or a municipal museum; rights to check)

WS-015.provenance_text: Jacques Hautelet, La Jolla, CA (by at least 2004); Robert H. Jackson by gift to the Cleveland Museum of Art (?–2015); The Cleveland Museum of Art (2015–)
WS-015.basis: Not an antiquity, so the 1970 test does not apply; made 1800 to mid-1900s in a colonised region and first recorded in 2004
WS-015.action: Replace with a throwing knife collected with a documented date and context; if none is licensed, show this one with its gap stated

WS-042.provenance_text: (Momtaz Islamic Art, London, England, sold to the Cleveland Museum of Art) (?–2004); The Cleveland Museum of Art (2004–)
WS-042.basis: First record 2004; an architectural element with no record of its building or its removal
WS-042.action: Drop as exemplar; the Iznik unit keeps WS-040 and WS-041

WS-091.provenance_text: [none published]; purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund, accessioned 9 September 1980
WS-091.action: Case, not exemplar: Luristan as the textbook case of objects without a findspot (F1.24; West Asia chapter). WS-092 carries the horse-gear point

WS-101.provenance_text: (Sara Tremayne, Ltd., London, UK, sold to the Cleveland Museum of Art) (?–1996); The Cleveland Museum of Art (1996–)
WS-101.action: Case, not exemplar. WS-102 (in Cleveland since 1959) becomes the steppe chapter's silk exemplar

WS-041.provenance_text: Sulzbach; Stora; Scarisbrick [no dates]; (Oliver Hoare Ltd., London, UK, sold to the Cleveland Museum of Art) (?-1995); The Cleveland Museum of Art (1995-)
WS-041.basis: Three named earlier owners, none dated; the test turns on whether any held it before 1970
WS-041.gap: Dates for the three named owners
WS-041.action: Keep as a provisional exemplar with its line shown; ask Cleveland for the owners' dates
